- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, use Config tool.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review changed code for reuse, quality, and efficiency, then fix any issues found.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled remote agents (triggers) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring remote agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/triggers.
- claude-api: Build, debug, and optimize Claude API / Anthropic SDK apps. Apps built with this skill should include prompt caching. Also handles migrating existing Claude API code between Claude model versions (4.5 → 4.6, 4.6 → 4.7, retired-model replacements).
TRIGGER when: code imports `anthropic`/`@anthropic-ai/sdk`; user asks for the Claude API, Anthropic SDK, or Managed Agents; user adds/modifies/tunes a Claude feature (caching, thinking, compaction, tool use, batch, files, citations, memory) or model (Opus/Sonnet/Haiku) in a file; questions about prompt caching / cache hit rate in an Anthropic SDK project.
SKIP: file imports `openai`/other-provider SDK, filename like `*-openai.py`/`*-generic.py`, provider-neutral code, general programming/ML.
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- review: Review a pull request
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<odoo>
    <data noupdate="0">

        <!-- ── MODULE CATEGORY ──────────────────────────────────────────────
             Creates a "Technical Services" section in the user settings form.
             This groups our three roles together cleanly.
        -->
        <record id="module_category_techservices" model="ir.module.category">
            <field name="name">Technical Services</field>
            <field name="description">Roles for the Technical Services facility</field>
            <field name="sequence">20</field>
        </record>

        <!-- ── TECHNICIAN ───────────────────────────────────────────────────
             Base role. Can:
               - View and edit their assigned repair orders
               - View repair history for all instruments (read-only)
               - Add parts and timesheet lines to their repairs
               - Browse inventory catalog (read-only by default)
               - Log their own timesheets

             Implied groups give them the minimum Odoo access needed
             without exposing Sales or Accounting.
        -->
        <record id="group_technician" model="res.groups">
            <field name="name">Technician</field>
            <field name="category_id" ref="module_category_techservices"/>
            <field name="implied_ids" eval="[
                (4, ref('stock.group_stock_user')),
                (4, ref('hr_timesheet.group_hr_timesheet_user')),
            ]"/>
        </record>

        <!-- ── SUPERVISOR ───────────────────────────────────────────────────
             Mid-level role. Can do everything a Technician can, plus:
               - View and edit all repair orders
               - Create and manage sale orders
               - Create and manage worktags
               - View invoices

             Implies Technician so supervisors automatically get all
             technician permissions.
        -->
        <record id="group_supervisor" model="res.groups">
            <field name="name">Supervisor</field>
            <field name="category_id" ref="module_category_techservices"/>
            <field name="implied_ids" eval="[
                (4, ref('techservices_groups.group_technician')),
                (4, ref('sales_team.group_sale_salesman')),
                (4, ref('hr_timesheet.group_hr_timesheet_approver')),
                (4, ref('account.group_account_invoice')),
            ]"/>
        </record>

        <!-- ── MANAGER ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
             Top-level role. Can do everything a Supervisor can, plus:
               - Full inventory management (create/edit products)
               - Validate worktags
               - Access all accounting and reporting features
               - Full timesheet administration

             Implies Supervisor so managers automatically get all
             supervisor and technician permissions.
        -->
        <record id="group_manager" model="res.groups">
            <field name="name">Manager</field>
            <field name="category_id" ref="module_category_techservices"/>
            <field name="implied_ids" eval="[
                (4, ref('techservices_groups.group_supervisor')),
                (4, ref('stock.group_stock_manager')),
                (4, ref('hr_timesheet.group_timesheet_manager')),
                (4, ref('account.group_account_manager')),
                (4, ref('base.group_system')),
            ]"/>
        </record>

    </data>
</odoo>

file.content:
services:

  odoo:
    image: odoo:18.0
    platform: linux/amd64
    container_name: odoo18_dev
    depends_on:
      - db
    ports:
      - "8069:8069"
      - "8072:8072"
    volumes:
      - ./custom_modules:/mnt/extra-addons
      - ./config/odoo.conf:/etc/odoo/odoo.conf
      - odoo_data:/var/lib/odoo
    environment:
      - HOST=db
      - USER=odoo
      - PASSWORD=odoo_dev_password
    restart: unless-stopped
    networks:
      - odoo_net

  db:
    image: postgres:15
    container_name: odoo18_db
    ports:
      - "5432:5432"
    volumes:
      - pg_data:/var/lib/postgresql/data
    environment:
      - POSTGRES_DB=postgres
      - POSTGRES_USER=odoo
      - POSTGRES_PASSWORD=odoo_dev_password
    restart: unless-stopped
    networks:
      - odoo_net

volumes:
  odoo_data:
  pg_data:

networks:
  odoo_net:
    driver: bridge

<?xml version="1.0" encoding="utf-8"?>
<odoo>
    <record id="view_service_worktag_list" model="ir.ui.view">
        <field name="name">service.worktag.list</field>
        <field name="model">service.worktag</field>
        <field name="arch" type="xml">
            <list string="Worktags">
                <field name="code"/>
                <field name="name"/>
                <field name="cost_centre"/>
                <field name="speedchart"/>
                <field name="client_category"/>
                <field name="partner_id"/>
                <field name="status" decoration-danger="status == 'inactive'" decoration-success="status == 'active'"/>
                <field name="validated" widget="boolean" decoration-success="validated == True" decoration-warning="validated == False"/>
            </list>
        </field>
    </record>

    <record id="view_service_worktag_form" model="ir.ui.view">
        <field name="name">service.worktag.form</field>
        <field name="model">service.worktag</field>
        <field name="arch" type="xml">
            <form string="Worktag">
                <sheet>
                    <group>
                        <group string="Identification">
                            <field name="code"/>
                            <field name="speedchart"/>
                            <field name="cost_centre"/>
                        </group>
                        <group string="Details">
                            <field name="name"/>
                            <field name="partner_id"/>
                            <field name="client_category"/>
                            <field name="status"/>
                            <field name="validated" groups="base.group_system"/>
                        </group>
                    </group>
                </sheet>
            </form>
        </field>
    </record>

    <record id="view_service_worktag_search" model="ir.ui.view">
        <field name="name">service.worktag.search</field>
        <field name="model">service.worktag</field>
        <field name="arch" type="xml">
            <search string="Search Worktags">
                <field name="code"/>
                <field name="name"/>
                <field name="speedchart"/>
                <field name="cost_centre"/>
                <field name="partner_id"/>
                <field name="client_category"/>
                <filter string="Active" name="active" domain="[('status', '=', 'active')]"/>
                <filter string="Inactive" name="inactive" domain="[('status', '=', 'inactive')]"/>
                <separator/>
                <filter string="Validated" name="validated" domain="[('validated', '=', True)]"/>
                <filter string="Not Validated" name="not_validated" domain="[('validated', '=', False)]"/>

Supervisor Role · MES Head

Supervisor Workflow Guide

Step-by-step reference for the full service lifecycle: from CRM opportunity intake through quotation, sale order, repair/work order, and invoice draft.

📅 Last updated: April 22, 2026 🔐 Role: Technical Services — Supervisor 🌐 Odoo 18 · localhost:8069 · DB: techservices

About This Guide

This document walks the MES Head (Supervisor role) through the complete end-to-end workflow for a new client service request. Screenshots are taken from a live Odoo 18 instance.

  • Login credentials: meshead@chem.ubc.ca
  • Role permissions: Supervisor inherits Technician rights, plus Sales, Timesheet Approver, and Account Invoicing access.
  • Worktag validation: A Manager must validate a worktag before an invoice can be posted. The Supervisor creates the order; the Manager approves the worktag.
1Login
›
2CRM Pipeline
›
3New Opportunity
›
4Add Notes & Contact
›
5New Quotation
›
6Service Type & Worktag
›
7Confirm → Sale Order
›
8Repair / Work Order
›
9Assign to Staff
›
10Invoice Draft
1

Log In as MES Head

Navigate to the Odoo login page and authenticate with the Supervisor account.

How To

  • Go to http://localhost:8069 and select the techservices database.
  • Enter email meshead@chem.ubc.ca and the assigned password, then click Log In.
  • The app opens at the Discuss → Inbox view. The top-right corner shows MES confirming the correct account.
ℹ️

The Supervisor role grants access to CRM, Sales, Repairs, Timesheets, and Invoicing views. Settings and inventory product creation are restricted to the Manager role.

Step 1 — Logged in as MES Head. Discuss inbox confirms correct session.
2

Open the CRM Pipeline

Navigate to the CRM module to view and manage service opportunities.

How To

  • Click the main menu grid (top-left) and open CRM, or navigate directly to /odoo/crm.
  • The Kanban pipeline shows stages: New, Needs information or actions, and Won.
  • The default filter is My Pipeline — showing only opportunities assigned to the current user.
💡

Switch to List view (icon top-right) for a faster overview when managing many opportunities at once.

Step 2 — CRM Pipeline in Kanban view showing current opportunities.
3

Create a New Opportunity & Add Internal Notes / New Contact

Open the full opportunity form, create a new client contact, and record intake details as internal notes.

How To — New Opportunity

  • Switch to List view and click the New button (top-left) to open the full opportunity form.
  • Enter a descriptive title in the opportunity name field (e.g. "Instrument Calibration & Repair Request").
  • The Salesperson is auto-set to MES Head.

How To — Add a New Contact

  • Click the Contact field and type the new client's name.
  • Select Create and edit… from the dropdown to open the contact dialog.
  • Select Individual, fill in Name, Phone, and Email, then click Save & Close.
  • The contact's email and phone will populate back on the opportunity form.
Step 3a — Creating a new Individual contact with phone and email from within the opportunity form.

How To — Add Internal Notes

  • With the contact saved, click the Internal Notes tab on the opportunity form.
  • Click inside the text area and type your intake notes — instrument details, priority, timeline, and any pre-authorized spend limits.
  • Click the save icon (cloud ☁) in the breadcrumb to save the record.
⚠️

Internal Notes are private — they are visible only to Odoo users, not to the client. Use the Send message button at the bottom for client-facing communication.

Step 3b — Opportunity form with new contact (Dr. Sarah Mitchell) and internal intake notes recorded.
4

Create a Quotation

Generate a quotation directly from the opportunity using the New Quotation button.

How To

  • From the saved opportunity, click New Quotation in the action bar (top-left).
  • The quotation form opens pre-filled with the customer and opportunity name.
  • The Expiration date defaults to 30 days out.
Step 4 — New Quotation form pre-populated from the opportunity. Service Type is required (highlighted in red if missing).
5

Add Service Type, Worktag & Labor Product

Select the appropriate service classification and billing worktag, then add the labor order line.

Service Type (required)

Click the Service Type dropdown and choose the category that best describes the work:

OptionWhen to use
RepairFixing or restoring a faulty instrument
ManufacturingBuilding or fabricating a component
MoveRelocating equipment between labs
InstallationSetting up new equipment on-site
MaintenanceScheduled preventive maintenance

Worktag

  • Click the Worktag field and type the code (e.g. CALREP-2026-001).
  • Worktags are filtered to those linked to the customer's commercial partner — only matching worktags appear.
  • When a worktag is selected, the Speedchart field auto-populates from the worktag record.
  • ⚠️ Worktags must be validated by a Manager before an invoice can be posted.
ℹ️

No worktags showing? The worktag's Company field must be set to the customer's commercial partner. If the customer is an individual with no parent company, the worktag's Company should match that individual's partner record. Ask the Manager to create the worktag if none exist.

Labor Product (Order Lines)

Click Add a product in the Order Lines tab and select the appropriate labor product. There are four labor products — choose based on client category:

ProductClient Category
Work order / repair order for Chemistry client – LaborUBC Chemistry department
Work order / repair order for UBC (external) client – LaborOther UBC departments
Work order / repair order for External to UBC or private client – LaborNon-UBC / private clients
Work order / repair order for Departmental service client – LaborInternal MES department service
Service TypeRepair WorktagCALREP-2026-001 SpeedchartMITCH-LAB (auto) Labor ProductExternal – Labor @ $100
Step 5 — Quotation complete: Service Type = Repair, Worktag = CALREP-2026-001, Speedchart auto-filled, labor product added with 12% GST+PST BC tax.
6

Confirm Quotation → Sales Order

Confirm the quotation to lock in pricing and generate the sales order and linked repair order.

How To

  • Review all fields, then click Confirm in the action bar.
  • The status bar moves to Sales Order and the record is assigned a number (e.g. S00081).
  • A Repairs smart button appears automatically — the system creates a linked repair order from the labor product line.
💡

Once confirmed, the order date and pricing are locked. To make changes, cancel and recreate, or use the Lock/Unlock controls visible to managers.

Access the auto-created repair order and review its details before assigning it to a technician.

How To

  • From the confirmed sales order, click the Repairs smart button (top bar).

How To

Return to the sales order and generate a draft invoice to be reviewed before posting.

A Manager must validate the worktag before this step succeeds. If the worktag's Validated checkbox is not checked, Odoo will block invoice creation with the error: "worktag has not been validated — a manager must check the Validated field on the worktag first."

"""
Build supervisor_workflow.docx from captured screenshots and step content.
Run: python3 build_docx.py
"""
from docx import Document
from docx.shared import Inches, Pt, RGBColor, Emu
from docx.enum.text import WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH
from docx.enum.table import WD_TABLE_ALIGNMENT, WD_ALIGN_VERTICAL
from docx.oxml.ns import qn
from docx.oxml import OxmlElement
import os, copy

SCREENSHOTS = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(__file__), "screenshots")

# ── Colours ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
PURPLE      = RGBColor(0x6B, 0x5B, 0x95)
PURPLE_DARK = RGBColor(0x4A, 0x3F, 0x72)
WHITE       = RGBColor(0xFF, 0xFF, 0xFF)
LIGHT_GREY  = RGBColor(0xF4, 0xF6, 0xF9)
WARN_BG     = RGBColor(0xFF, 0xF8, 0xE6)
INFO_BG     = RGBColor(0xEE, 0xF4, 0xFF)
TIP_BG      = RGBColor(0xED, 0xFB, 0xF3)
GREY_TEXT   = RGBColor(0x66, 0x66, 0x66)


# ── Low-level XML helpers ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
def set_cell_bg(cell, rgb: RGBColor):
    tc   = cell._tc
    tcPr = tc.get_or_add_tcPr()
    shd  = OxmlElement("w:shd")
    hex_color = f"{rgb.red:02X}{rgb.green:02X}{rgb.blue:02X}"
    shd.set(qn("w:val"),   "clear")
    shd.set(qn("w:color"), "auto")
    shd.set(qn("w:fill"),  hex_color)
    tcPr.append(shd)


def set_run_color(run, rgb: RGBColor):
    run.font.color.rgb = rgb


def set_para_spacing(para, before=0, after=0, line=None):
    pf = para.paragraph_format
    pf.space_before = Pt(before)
    pf.space_after  = Pt(after)
    if line:
        from docx.shared import Pt as _Pt
        pf.line_spacing = _Pt(line)


def add_horizontal_rule(doc):
    p   = doc.add_paragraph()
    pPr = p._p.get_or_add_pPr()
    pb  = OxmlElement("w:pBdr")
    bot = OxmlElement("w:bottom")
    bot.set(qn("w:val"),   "single")
    bot.set(qn("w:sz"),    "4")
    bot.set(qn("w:space"), "1")
    bot.set(qn("w:color"), "CCCCCC")
    pb.append(bot)
    pPr.append(pb)
    set_para_spacing(p, before=2, after=2)
    return p


# ── Reusable paragraph builders ───────────────────────────────────────────────
def add_heading(doc, text, level=1, color=PURPLE_DARK):
    h = doc.add_heading(text, level=level)
    h.style.font.color.rgb = color
    for run in h.runs:
        run.font.color.rgb = color
    set_para_spacing(h, before=14 if level == 1 else 10, after=4)
    return h


def add_body(doc, text, color=None, italic=False, bold=False):
    p   = doc.add_paragraph()
    run = p.add_run(text)
    run.font.size = Pt(10.5)
    if color:
        run.font.color.rgb = color
    run.italic = italic
    run.bold   = bold
    set_para_spacing(p, before=2, after=4)
    return p


def add_bullet(doc, text, bold_prefix=None):
    p = doc.add_paragraph(style="List Bullet")
    p.paragraph_format.left_indent = Inches(0.3)
    p.paragraph_format.space_after  = Pt(3)
    if bold_prefix:
        r = p.add_run(bold_prefix)
        r.bold = True
        r.font.size = Pt(10.5)
        p.add_run(text).font.size = Pt(10.5)
    else:
        p.add_run(text).font.size = Pt(10.5)
    return p


def add_callout(doc, icon, title, body_text, bg: RGBColor):
    tbl = doc.add_table(rows=1, cols=2)
    tbl.style = "Table Grid"
    tbl.alignment = WD_TABLE_ALIGNMENT.LEFT
    tbl.columns[0].width = Inches(0.45)
    tbl.columns[1].width = Inches(5.85)
    icon_cell, text_cell = tbl.rows[0].cells
    set_cell_bg(icon_cell, bg)
    set_cell_bg(text_cell, bg)
    # icon
    ip = icon_cell.paragraphs[0]
    ip.alignment = WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH.CENTER
    ir = ip.add_run(icon)
    ir.font.size = Pt(14)
    # text
    tp = text_cell.paragraphs[0]
    if title:
        tb = tp.add_run(f"{title}  ")
        tb.bold = True
        tb.font.size = Pt(10)
    tp.add_run(body_text).font.size = Pt(10)
    # borders: remove grid lines, keep left accent
    for cell in (icon_cell, text_cell):
        tc   = cell._tc
        tcPr = tc.get_or_add_tcPr()
        tcBdr = OxmlElement("w:tcBdr")
        for side in ("top", "bottom", "right", "left", "insideH", "insideV"):
            el = OxmlElement(f"w:{side}")
            el.set(qn("w:val"),   "none")
            el.set(qn("w:sz"),    "0")
            el.set(qn("w:space"), "0")
            el.set(qn("w:color"), "auto")
            tcBdr.append(el)
        tcPr.append(tcBdr)
    p = doc.add_paragraph()
    set_para_spacing(p, before=0, after=4)
    return tbl

    path = os.path.join(SCREENSHOTS, filename)
    if not os.path.exists(path):
        add_body(doc, f"[Screenshot not found: {filename}]", color=RGBColor(0xCC, 0, 0))
        return
    doc.add_picture(path, width=Inches(6.3))
    cap = doc.add_paragraph(caption)
    cap.alignment = WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH.CENTER
    for run in cap.runs:
        run.font.size   = Pt(9)
        run.font.italic = True
        run.font.color.rgb = GREY_TEXT
    set_para_spacing(cap, before=2, after=10)


def add_two_col_table(doc, headers, rows, col_widths=None):
    n = len(headers)
    tbl = doc.add_table(rows=1 + len(rows), cols=n)
    tbl.style = "Table Grid"
    tbl.alignment = WD_TABLE_ALIGNMENT.LEFT
    # default widths
    if col_widths is None:
        w = Inches(6.3 / n)
        col_widths = [w] * n
    for i, col in enumerate(tbl.columns):
        col.width = col_widths[i]
    # header row
    hdr = tbl.rows[0]
    for i, h in enumerate(headers):
        cell = hdr.cells[i]
        set_cell_bg(cell, PURPLE)
        p = cell.paragraphs[0]
        r = p.add_run(h)
        r.bold = True
        r.font.color.rgb = WHITE
        r.font.size = Pt(10)
    # data rows
    for ri, row in enumerate(rows):
        for ci, val in enumerate(row):
            cell = tbl.rows[ri + 1].cells[ci]
            if ri % 2 == 1:
                set_cell_bg(cell, RGBColor(0xFA, 0xFA, 0xFA))
            p = cell.paragraphs[0]
            if isinstance(val, tuple):  # (bold_part, rest)
                rb = p.add_run(val[0])
                rb.bold = True
                rb.font.size = Pt(10)
                p.add_run(val[1]).font.size = Pt(10)
            else:
                p.add_run(val).font.size = Pt(10)
    p = doc.add_paragraph()
    set_para_spacing(p, before=0, after=6)
    return tbl

    title_cell.paragraphs[0].runs[-1].font.size = Pt(9.5)
    # remove borders

    p = doc.add_paragraph()

"""
Build supervisor_workflow.docx from captured screenshots and step content.
Run: python3 build_docx.py
"""
from docx import Document
from docx.shared import Inches, Pt, RGBColor, Emu
from docx.enum.text import WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH
from docx.enum.table import WD_TABLE_ALIGNMENT, WD_ALIGN_VERTICAL
from docx.oxml.ns import qn
from docx.oxml import OxmlElement
import os, copy

SCREENSHOTS = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(__file__), "screenshots")

# ── Colours ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
PURPLE      = RGBColor(0x6B, 0x5B, 0x95)
PURPLE_DARK = RGBColor(0x4A, 0x3F, 0x72)
WHITE       = RGBColor(0xFF, 0xFF, 0xFF)
LIGHT_GREY  = RGBColor(0xF4, 0xF6, 0xF9)
WARN_BG     = RGBColor(0xFF, 0xF8, 0xE6)
INFO_BG     = RGBColor(0xEE, 0xF4, 0xFF)
TIP_BG      = RGBColor(0xED, 0xFB, 0xF3)
GREY_TEXT   = RGBColor(0x66, 0x66, 0x66)


# ── Low-level XML helpers ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
def set_cell_bg(cell, rgb: RGBColor):
    tc   = cell._tc
    tcPr = tc.get_or_add_tcPr()
    shd  = OxmlElement("w:shd")
    hex_color = f"{rgb.red:02X}{rgb.green:02X}{rgb.blue:02X}"
    shd.set(qn("w:val"),   "clear")
    shd.set(qn("w:color"), "auto")
    shd.set(qn("w:fill"),  hex_color)
    tcPr.append(shd)


def set_run_color(run, rgb: RGBColor):
    run.font.color.rgb = rgb


def set_para_spacing(para, before=0, after=0, line=None):
    pf = para.paragraph_format
    pf.space_before = Pt(before)
    pf.space_after  = Pt(after)
    if line:
        from docx.shared import Pt as _Pt
        pf.line_spacing = _Pt(line)


def add_horizontal_rule(doc):
    p   = doc.add_paragraph()
    pPr = p._p.get_or_add_pPr()
    pb  = OxmlElement("w:pBdr")
    bot = OxmlElement("w:bottom")
    bot.set(qn("w:val"),   "single")
    bot.set(qn("w:sz"),    "4")
    bot.set(qn("w:space"), "1")
    bot.set(qn("w:color"), "CCCCCC")
    pb.append(bot)
    pPr.append(pb)
    set_para_spacing(p, before=2, after=2)
    return p


# ── Reusable paragraph builders ───────────────────────────────────────────────
def add_heading(doc, text, level=1, color=PURPLE_DARK):
    h = doc.add_heading(text, level=level)
    h.style.font.color.rgb = color
    for run in h.runs:
        run.font.color.rgb = color
    set_para_spacing(h, before=14 if level == 1 else 10, after=4)
    return h


def add_body(doc, text, color=None, italic=False, bold=False):
    p   = doc.add_paragraph()
    run = p.add_run(text)
    run.font.size = Pt(10.5)
    if color:
        run.font.color.rgb = color
    run.italic = italic
    run.bold   = bold
    set_para_spacing(p, before=2, after=4)
    return p


def add_bullet(doc, text, bold_prefix=None):
    p = doc.add_paragraph(style="List Bullet")
    p.paragraph_format.left_indent = Inches(0.3)
    p.paragraph_format.space_after  = Pt(3)
    if bold_prefix:
        r = p.add_run(bold_prefix)
        r.bold = True
        r.font.size = Pt(10.5)
        p.add_run(text).font.size = Pt(10.5)
    else:
        p.add_run(text).font.size = Pt(10.5)
    return p


def add_callout(doc, icon, title, body_text, bg: RGBColor):
    tbl = doc.add_table(rows=1, cols=2)
    tbl.style = "Table Grid"
    tbl.alignment = WD_TABLE_ALIGNMENT.LEFT
    tbl.columns[0].width = Inches(0.45)
    tbl.columns[1].width = Inches(5.85)
    icon_cell, text_cell = tbl.rows[0].cells
    set_cell_bg(icon_cell, bg)
    set_cell_bg(text_cell, bg)
    # icon
    ip = icon_cell.paragraphs[0]
    ip.alignment = WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH.CENTER
    ir = ip.add_run(icon)
    ir.font.size = Pt(14)
    # text
    tp = text_cell.paragraphs[0]
    if title:
        tb = tp.add_run(f"{title}  ")
        tb.bold = True
        tb.font.size = Pt(10)
    tp.add_run(body_text).font.size = Pt(10)
    # borders: remove grid lines, keep left accent
    for cell in (icon_cell, text_cell):
        tc   = cell._tc
        tcPr = tc.get_or_add_tcPr()
        tcBdr = OxmlElement("w:tcBdr")
        for side in ("top", "bottom", "right", "left", "insideH", "insideV"):
            el = OxmlElement(f"w:{side}")
            el.set(qn("w:val"),   "none")
            el.set(qn("w:sz"),    "0")
            el.set(qn("w:space"), "0")
            el.set(qn("w:color"), "auto")
            tcBdr.append(el)
        tcPr.append(tcBdr)
    p = doc.add_paragraph()
    set_para_spacing(p, before=0, after=4)
    return tbl


def add_screenshot(doc, filename, caption):
    path = os.path.join(SCREENSHOTS, filename)
    if not os.path.exists(path):
        add_body(doc, f"[Screenshot not found: {filename}]", color=RGBColor(0xCC, 0, 0))
        return
    doc.add_picture(path, width=Inches(6.3))
    cap = doc.add_paragraph(caption)
    cap.alignment = WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH.CENTER
    for run in cap.runs:
        run.font.size   = Pt(9)
        run.font.italic = True
        run.font.color.rgb = GREY_TEXT
    set_para_spacing(cap, before=2, after=10)


def add_two_col_table(doc, headers, rows, col_widths=None):
    n = len(headers)
    tbl = doc.add_table(rows=1 + len(rows), cols=n)
    tbl.style = "Table Grid"
    tbl.alignment = WD_TABLE_ALIGNMENT.LEFT
    # default widths
    if col_widths is None:
        w = Inches(6.3 / n)
        col_widths = [w] * n
    for i, col in enumerate(tbl.columns):
        col.width = col_widths[i]
    # header row
    hdr = tbl.rows[0]
    for i, h in enumerate(headers):
        cell = hdr.cells[i]
        set_cell_bg(cell, PURPLE)
        p = cell.paragraphs[0]
        r = p.add_run(h)
        r.bold = True
        r.font.color.rgb = WHITE
        r.font.size = Pt(10)
    # data rows
    for ri, row in enumerate(rows):
        for ci, val in enumerate(row):
            cell = tbl.rows[ri + 1].cells[ci]
            if ri % 2 == 1:
                set_cell_bg(cell, RGBColor(0xFA, 0xFA, 0xFA))
            p = cell.paragraphs[0]
            if isinstance(val, tuple):  # (bold_part, rest)
                rb = p.add_run(val[0])
                rb.bold = True
                rb.font.size = Pt(10)
                p.add_run(val[1]).font.size = Pt(10)
            else:
                p.add_run(val).font.size = Pt(10)
    p = doc.add_paragraph()
    set_para_spacing(p, before=0, after=6)
    return tbl

    # remove borders

            tcBdr.append(el)
        tcPr.append(tcBdr)
    p = doc.add_paragraph()
    set_para_spacing(p, before=0, after=6)

name: Odoo Dev Environment
description: Key facts about the local Odoo development setup at ~/Documents/Developer/odoo-dev
type: project
originSessionId: 36785d4c-7291-4fc6-a025-f92af3be6ee8

Docker Compose project at `/Users/sebastianmedrano/Documents/Developer/odoo-dev`. Two containers: `odoo18_dev` (Odoo 18.0) and `odoo18_db` (Postgres 15). Runs on `localhost:8069`.

**Why:** Active Odoo customization project with custom modules.

**How to apply:** Always use `-d techservices` (not `-d odoo`) for all `odoo -u/-i` commands. The live database is `techservices`. Custom modules live in `custom_modules/` which is mounted at `/mnt/extra-addons` inside the container.

After every module upgrade, restart the container:
```
docker compose exec odoo odoo -u <module> --stop-after-init -d techservices
docker compose restart odoo
```

<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<odoo>
    <data noupdate="0">

        <!-- ── MODULE CATEGORY ──────────────────────────────────────────────
             Creates a "Technical Services" section in the user settings form.
             This groups our three roles together cleanly.
        -->
        <record id="module_category_techservices" model="ir.module.category">
            <field name="name">Technical Services</field>
            <field name="description">Roles for the Technical Services facility</field>
            <field name="sequence">20</field>
        </record>

        <!-- ── TECHNICIAN ───────────────────────────────────────────────────
             Base role. Can:
               - View and edit their assigned repair orders
               - View repair history for all instruments (read-only)
               - Add parts and timesheet lines to their repairs
               - Browse inventory catalog (read-only by default)
               - Log their own timesheets

             Implied groups give them the minimum Odoo access needed
             without exposing Sales or Accounting.
        -->
        <record id="group_technician" model="res.groups">
            <field name="name">Technician</field>
            <field name="category_id" ref="module_category_techservices"/>
            <field name="implied_ids" eval="[
                (4, ref('stock.group_stock_user')),
                (4, ref('hr_timesheet.group_hr_timesheet_user')),
            ]"/>
        </record>

        <!-- ── SUPERVISOR ───────────────────────────────────────────────────
             Mid-level role. Can do everything a Technician can, plus:
               - View and edit all repair orders
               - Create and manage sale orders
               - Create and manage worktags
               - View invoices

             Implies Technician so supervisors automatically get all
             technician permissions.
        -->
        <record id="group_supervisor" model="res.groups">
            <field name="name">Supervisor</field>
            <field name="category_id" ref="module_category_techservices"/>
            <field name="implied_ids" eval="[
                (4, ref('techservices_groups.group_technician')),
                (4, ref('sales_team.group_sale_salesman')),
                (4, ref('hr_timesheet.group_hr_timesheet_approver')),
                (4, ref('account.group_account_invoice')),
            ]"/>
        </record>

        <!-- ── MANAGER ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
             Top-level role. Can do everything a Supervisor can, plus:
               - Full inventory management (create/edit products)
               - Validate worktags
               - Access all accounting and reporting features
               - Full timesheet administration

             Implies Supervisor so managers automatically get all
             supervisor and technician permissions.
        -->
        <record id="group_manager" model="res.groups">
            <field name="name">Manager</field>
            <field name="category_id" ref="module_category_techservices"/>
            <field name="implied_ids" eval="[
                (4, ref('techservices_groups.group_supervisor')),
                (4, ref('stock.group_stock_manager')),
                (4, ref('hr_timesheet.group_timesheet_manager')),
                (4, ref('account.group_account_manager')),
                (4, ref('base.group_system')),
            ]"/>
        </record>

    </data>
</odoo>

services:

  odoo:
    image: odoo:18.0
    platform: linux/amd64
    container_name: odoo18_dev
    depends_on:
      - db
    ports:
      - "8069:8069"
      - "8072:8072"
    volumes:
      - ./custom_modules:/mnt/extra-addons
      - ./config/odoo.conf:/etc/odoo/odoo.conf
      - odoo_data:/var/lib/odoo
    environment:
      - HOST=db
      - USER=odoo
      - PASSWORD=odoo_dev_password
    restart: unless-stopped
    networks:
      - odoo_net

  db:
    image: postgres:15
    container_name: odoo18_db
    ports:
      - "5432:5432"
    volumes:
      - pg_data:/var/lib/postgresql/data
    environment:
      - POSTGRES_DB=postgres
      - POSTGRES_USER=odoo
      - POSTGRES_PASSWORD=odoo_dev_password
    restart: unless-stopped
    networks:
      - odoo_net

volumes:
  odoo_data:
  pg_data:

networks:
  odoo_net:
    driver: bridge

"""
Build supervisor_workflow.docx from captured screenshots and step content.
Run: python3 build_docx.py
"""
from docx import Document
from docx.shared import Inches, Pt, RGBColor, Emu
from docx.enum.text import WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH
from docx.enum.table import WD_TABLE_ALIGNMENT, WD_ALIGN_VERTICAL
from docx.oxml.ns import qn
from docx.oxml import OxmlElement
import os, copy

SCREENSHOTS = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(__file__), "screenshots")

# ── Colours ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
PURPLE      = RGBColor(0x6B, 0x5B, 0x95)
PURPLE_DARK = RGBColor(0x4A, 0x3F, 0x72)
WHITE       = RGBColor(0xFF, 0xFF, 0xFF)
LIGHT_GREY  = RGBColor(0xF4, 0xF6, 0xF9)
WARN_BG     = RGBColor(0xFF, 0xF8, 0xE6)
INFO_BG     = RGBColor(0xEE, 0xF4, 0xFF)
TIP_BG      = RGBColor(0xED, 0xFB, 0xF3)
GREY_TEXT   = RGBColor(0x66, 0x66, 0x66)


# ── Low-level XML helpers ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
def set_cell_bg(cell, rgb: RGBColor):
    tc   = cell._tc
    tcPr = tc.get_or_add_tcPr()
    shd  = OxmlElement("w:shd")
    hex_color = f"{rgb.red:02X}{rgb.green:02X}{rgb.blue:02X}"
    shd.set(qn("w:val"),   "clear")
    shd.set(qn("w:color"), "auto")
    shd.set(qn("w:fill"),  hex_color)
    tcPr.append(shd)


def set_run_color(run, rgb: RGBColor):
    run.font.color.rgb = rgb


def set_para_spacing(para, before=0, after=0, line=None):
    pf = para.paragraph_format
    pf.space_before = Pt(before)
    pf.space_after  = Pt(after)
    if line:
        from docx.shared import Pt as _Pt
        pf.line_spacing = _Pt(line)

        cr.commit()
        print('Done.')
    else:

"

All restricted menus now require the **Technical Services / Manager** group. Here's what changed and why it now works:

**Root cause:** MES Head's user account had Inventory access set to "Administrator" (via the user settings form at some point), which placed them in `stock.group_stock_manager`. Our original restriction was gated on that same group, so it had no effect on them.

**Fix 1 — Restriction uses our own group:** All 19 restricted menus now require `techservices_groups.group_manager` instead of `stock.group_stock_manager`. This gives us full control — only users with our Manager role see those sections.

**Fix 2 — User data corrected:** Removed MES Head (and scanned for any other Supervisor/Technician users) from `stock.group_stock_manager`, keeping them in `stock.group_stock_user` as intended.

Technicians and Supervisors will now see only **Inventory → Products** when they open the Inventory app.

Have the MES Head user (or you, if you're testing as them):

1. **Hard refresh**: `Cmd + Shift + R` (Mac) or `Ctrl + Shift + R` (Windows/Linux) while on the Odoo page
2. Or **log out and log back in** — this forces a fresh menu load

If that doesn't work, open DevTools → Application → Storage → Clear site data, then reload.

<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<odoo>
    <data>
        <!--
            Hide fields and buttons on the product form for Technician / Supervisor roles.
            Each record targets the specific inherited view that introduces the element.
            Setting groups="techservices_groups.group_manager" makes the element invisible
            to all users who are not in the Manager role.
        -->

        <!-- ══ 1. Base product form ──────────────────────────────────────────────
             Hides: Print Labels (header button)
             Parent: product.product_template_form_view
        -->
        <record id="product_template_hide_print_labels" model="ir.ui.view">
            <field name="name">product.template.hide.print.labels.techservices</field>
            <field name="model">product.template</field>
            <field name="inherit_id" ref="product.product_template_form_view"/>
            <field name="arch" type="xml">
                <xpath expr="//button[@name='action_open_label_layout']" position="attributes">
                    <attribute name="groups">techservices_groups.group_manager</attribute>
                </xpath>
            </field>
        </record>

        <!-- ══ 2. product_template_only_form_view ───────────────────────────────
             Hides: Reference (default_code), Barcode
             Parent: product.product_template_only_form_view
        -->
        <record id="product_template_hide_ref_barcode" model="ir.ui.view">
            <field name="name">product.template.hide.ref.barcode.techservices</field>
            <field name="model">product.template</field>
            <field name="inherit_id" ref="product.product_template_only_form_view"/>
            <field name="arch" type="xml">
                <xpath expr="//field[@name='default_code'][@string='Reference']" position="attributes">
                    <attribute name="groups">techservices_groups.group_manager</attribute>
                </xpath>
                <xpath expr="//field[@name='barcode']" position="attributes">
                    <attribute name="groups">techservices_groups.group_manager</attribute>
                </xpath>
            </field>
        </record>

        <!-- ══ 3. account product form inherit ──────────────────────────────────
             Hides: Purchase checkbox (field + label)
             Parent: account.product_template_form_view
        -->
        <record id="product_template_hide_purchase_ok" model="ir.ui.view">
            <field name="name">product.template.hide.purchase.techservices</field>
            <field name="model">product.template</field>
            <field name="inherit_id" ref="account.product_template_form_view"/>
            <field name="arch" type="xml">
                <xpath expr="//field[@name='purchase_ok']" position="attributes">
                    <attribute name="groups">techservices_groups.group_manager</attribute>
                </xpath>
                <xpath expr="//label[@for='purchase_ok']" position="attributes">
                    <attribute name="groups">techservices_groups.group_manager</attribute>
                </xpath>
            </field>
        </record>

        <!-- ══ 4. sale product form inherit ─────────────────────────────────────
             Hides: Invoicing Policy
             Parent: sale.product_template_form_view
        -->
        <record id="product_template_hide_invoice_policy" model="ir.ui.view">
            <field name="name">product.template.hide.invoice.policy.techservices</field>
            <field name="model">product.template</field>
            <field name="inherit_id" ref="sale.product_template_form_view"/>
            <field name="arch" type="xml">
                <xpath expr="//field[@name='invoice_policy']" position="attributes">
                    <attribute name="groups">techservices_groups.group_manager</attribute>
                </xpath>
            </field>
        </record>

        <!-- ══ 5. repair product form inherit ───────────────────────────────────
             Hides: Create Repair checkbox
             Parent: repair.view_product_template_form_inherit_repair
        -->
        <record id="product_template_hide_create_repair" model="ir.ui.view">
            <field name="name">product.template.hide.create.repair.techservices</field>
            <field name="model">product.template</field>
            <field name="inherit_id" ref="repair.view_product_template_form_inherit_repair"/>
            <field name="arch" type="xml">
                <xpath expr="//field[@name='create_repair']" position="attributes">
                    <attribute name="groups">techservices_groups.group_manager</attribute>
                </xpath>
            </field>
        </record>

        <!-- ══ 6. stock procurement buttons ─────────────────────────────────────
             Hides: Replenish (header), Forecasted, Reordering Rules (×2), In/Out
             Parent: stock.product_template_form_view_procurement_button
        -->
        <record id="product_template_hide_stock_buttons" model="ir.ui.view">
            <field name="name">product.template.hide.stock.buttons.techservices</field>
            <field name="model">product.template</field>
            <field name="inherit_id" ref="stock.product_template_form_view_procurement_button"/>
            <field name="arch" type="xml">
                <!-- Replenish header button -->
                <xpath expr="//button[@string='Replenish']" position="attributes">
                    <attribute name="groups">techservices_groups.group_manager</attribute>
                </xpath>
                <!-- Forecasted smart button -->
                <xpath expr="//button[@name='action_product_tmpl_forecast_report']" position="attributes">
                    <attribute name="groups">techservices_groups.group_manager</attribute>
                </xpath>
                <!-- Reordering Rules smart button (single rule) -->
                <xpath expr="//button[@name='action_view_orderpoints'][1]" position="attributes">
                    <attribute name="groups">techservices_groups.group_manager</attribute>
                </xpath>
                <!-- Reordering Rules smart button (multiple rules) -->
                <xpath expr="//button[@name='action_view_orderpoints'][2]" position="attributes">
                    <attribute name="groups">techservices_groups.group_manager</attribute>
                </xpath>
                <!-- In / Out smart button -->
                <xpath expr="//button[@name='action_view_stock_move_lines']" position="attributes">
                    <attribute name="groups">techservices_groups.group_manager</attribute>
                </xpath>
            </field>
        </record>

    </data>
</odoo>

---

Custom module at `custom_modules/techservices_groups`. Key things built:

**Roles** (security/techservices_groups.xml):
- Technician → implies stock.group_stock_user + hr_timesheet user
- Supervisor → implies Technician + sales salesman + timesheet approver + account invoicing
- Manager → implies Supervisor + stock manager + timesheet manager + account manager + base.group_system

**Inventory menu restrictions** (views/inventory_menu_restrictions.xml):
- Technician/Supervisor see only Inventory → Products section
- Overview, Operations, Reporting, Configuration restricted to `techservices_groups.group_manager`
- Uses our own Manager group, NOT stock.group_stock_manager (learned: stock group can be directly assigned to users independently)

**Product form restrictions** (views/product_form_restrictions.xml):
- Hidden from Technician/Supervisor via `groups="techservices_groups.group_manager"`:
  - Purchase checkbox, Invoicing Policy, Create Repair, Reference, Barcode
  - Forecasted, Reordering Rules (×2), In/Out smart buttons
  - Replenish header button (targeted by numeric action ID 428, not string)
  - Print Labels button
- Spans across 5 separate inherited views (product, account, sale, repair, stock)

**Product form new fields** (models/product_template.py + views/product_template_fields.xml):
- `x_make` (Char) — brand/manufacturer
- `x_supplier_id` (Many2one → res.partner, domain: is_supplier=True) — filtered to Supplier contacts only
- `x_supplier_part_number` (Char) — vendor part code
- Placed in group_general after the type field, visible to all roles

**Supplier contact type** (models/res_partner.py):
- Added `is_supplier = fields.Boolean(store=True)` to res.partner
- Extended `company_type` selection with `('supplier', 'Supplier')` third option
- Overrode `_compute_company_type`, `_write_company_type`, `onchange_company_type`
- Supplier contacts have is_company=True + is_supplier=True
- Radio button on contact form shows automatically (no view changes needed)

**Why:** `ondelete` for selection_add must be a lambda (not 'set default') when the base field has no default.
**How to apply:** When restricting menus, always use our custom group not stock groups — users can be manually assigned to stock groups independently of our role hierarchy.

**Filters**
| Filter | What it shows |
|---|---|
| Services | Products with type = Service |
| Goods | Products with type = Consumable/Storable |
| Combo | Products with type = Combo |
| Inventory Management | Storable products (tracked in stock) |
| Sales | Products marked as "Can be Sold" |
| Purchase | Products marked as "Can be Purchased" |
| Available Products | Products with qty on hand > 0 |
| Negative Forecasted Quantity | Products with forecasted qty < 0 |
| Favorites | Products marked as favorite |
| Warnings | Products with active activity warnings |
| Archived | Inactive/archived products |

**Group By**
| Option | Groups by |
|---|---|
| Product Type | service / consumable / storable |
| Product Category | internal category (categ_id) |

The default filter applied when opening the list from the Inventory > Products menu is **Sales** (sale_ok = True), set via `search_default_filter_to_sell` in the action context.

                <field name="categ_id" filter_domain="[('categ_id', 'child_of', raw_value)]"/>
                <field name="product_template_attribute_value_ids"
                       groups="product.group_product_variant"/>
                <field name="product_tmpl_id" string="Product Template"/>
                <!-- Filter -->
                <filter string="Favorites" name="favorites" domain="[('is_favorite', '=', True)]"/>
                <separator/>
                <filter string="Services" name="services" domain="[('type', '=', 'service')]"/>
                <filter string="Goods"
                        name="goods"
                        domain="[('type', '=', 'consu')]"/>
                <!-- Group By -->
                <group expand="1" string="Group By">
                    <filter string="Product Type" name="type" context="{'group_by':'type'}"/>
                    <filter string="Product Category"
                            name="categ_id"

                           enable_counters="1"
                           select="multi"/>

            </search>
        </field>
    </record>

content.text: The access rule is not noupdate, so I can modify it. The cleanest Odoo approach: strip `create` from the base `stock.group_stock_user` rule (which Technicians use), then grant it back explicitly to the Supervisor group (which Supervisors and Managers both inherit). Additive permission logic means Supervisors get create via their own rule while Technicians don't.

input.content:
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<odoo>
    <data noupdate="0">

        <!--
            REPAIR ORDER ACCESS CONTROL
            ════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

            Goal: Technicians should not be able to create new repair orders
            directly from the Repairs list view (the "New" button must be
            hidden for them).

            How Odoo permission logic works here:
            ─ ir.model.access rules are ADDITIVE (OR logic): a user gets a
              permission if ANY group they belong to grants it.
            ─ There is no "deny" rule, so we cannot block create for one group
              while another grants it.

            Strategy:
            1. Remove perm_create from the existing stock.group_stock_user rule
               (repair.access_repair_user).  Technicians only belong to
               stock.group_stock_user, so they lose the ability to create
               repair orders, and Odoo automatically hides the "New" button.
            2. Add a new rule that grants perm_create to
               techservices_groups.group_supervisor.  Since Supervisors and
               Managers both inherit group_supervisor via implied_ids, they
               retain full create access through this rule.
        -->

        <!-- 1. Strip create permission from the base Inventory/User rule.
                Technicians only belong to stock.group_stock_user, so after
                this change they will no longer be able to create repair orders. -->
        <record id="repair.access_repair_user" model="ir.model.access">
            <field name="perm_create" eval="False"/>
        </record>

        <!-- 2. Grant full access (including create) to the Supervisor role.
                techservices_groups.group_supervisor is implied by group_manager,
                so Managers also benefit from this rule automatically. -->
        <record id="access_repair_order_supervisor" model="ir.model.access">
            <field name="name">repair.order.techservices.supervisor</field>
            <field name="model_id" ref="repair.model_repair_order"/>
            <field name="group_id" ref="techservices_groups.group_supervisor"/>
            <field name="perm_read" eval="True"/>
            <field name="perm_write" eval="True"/>
            <field name="perm_create" eval="True"/>
            <field name="perm_unlink" eval="True"/>
        </record>

    </data>
</odoo>

content.text: Both "Post" and "Confirm" buttons share `name="action_post"` — a single XPath will catch both. I'll also add a Python-level guard on `action_post()` so the restriction holds even if the button is accessed through another route:

input.content:
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<odoo>
    <data>
        <!--
            INVOICE CONFIRM / POST BUTTON RESTRICTION
            ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

            Goal: Supervisors can create draft invoices but cannot post them.
            Only the Manager role should be able to move an invoice from
            Draft → Posted by clicking Confirm (customer invoices) or Post
            (journal entries).

            Both the "Confirm" and "Post" buttons call action_post() and share
            name="action_post", so a single XPath catches both.  We replace the
            existing groups="account.group_account_invoice" with
            groups="techservices_groups.group_manager", which is implied by
            the Manager role only.

            A matching server-side guard in models/account_move.py ensures the
            restriction also applies if action_post() is triggered outside the
            UI (e.g. RPC call or automated action).
        -->
        <record id="account_move_hide_post_supervisor" model="ir.ui.view">
            <field name="name">account.move.hide.post.supervisor.techservices</field>
            <field name="model">account.move</field>
            <field name="inherit_id" ref="account.view_move_form"/>
            <field name="arch" type="xml">
                <!-- Restrict both the "Confirm" (invoice) and "Post" (journal entry)
                     buttons to the Manager role.  Supervisors will see neither button
                     and therefore cannot transition an invoice out of Draft state. -->
                <xpath expr="//button[@name='action_post']" position="attributes">
                    <attribute name="groups">techservices_groups.group_manager</attribute>
                </xpath>
            </field>
        </record>
    </data>
</odoo>

<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<odoo>
    <data noupdate="0">

        <!-- ── MODULE CATEGORY ──────────────────────────────────────────────
             Creates a "Technical Services" section in the user settings form.
             This groups our three roles together cleanly.
        -->
        <record id="module_category_techservices" model="ir.module.category">
            <field name="name">Technical Services</field>
            <field name="description">Roles for the Technical Services facility</field>
            <field name="sequence">20</field>
        </record>

        <!-- ── TECHNICIAN ───────────────────────────────────────────────────
             Base role. Can:
               - View and edit their assigned repair orders
               - View repair history for all instruments (read-only)
               - Add parts and timesheet lines to their repairs
               - Browse inventory catalog (read-only by default)
               - Log their own timesheets

             Implied groups give them the minimum Odoo access needed
             without exposing Sales or Accounting.
        -->
        <record id="group_technician" model="res.groups">
            <field name="name">Technician</field>
            <field name="category_id" ref="module_category_techservices"/>
            <field name="implied_ids" eval="[
                (4, ref('stock.group_stock_user')),
                (4, ref('hr_timesheet.group_hr_timesheet_user')),
            ]"/>
        </record>

        <!-- ── SUPERVISOR ───────────────────────────────────────────────────
             Mid-level role. Can do everything a Technician can, plus:
               - View and edit all repair orders
               - Create and manage sale orders
               - Create and manage worktags
               - View invoices

             Implies Technician so supervisors automatically get all
             technician permissions.
        -->
        <record id="group_supervisor" model="res.groups">
            <field name="name">Supervisor</field>
            <field name="category_id" ref="module_category_techservices"/>
            <field name="implied_ids" eval="[
                (4, ref('techservices_groups.group_technician')),
                (4, ref('sales_team.group_sale_salesman')),
                (4, ref('hr_timesheet.group_hr_timesheet_approver')),
                (4, ref('account.group_account_invoice')),
            ]"/>
        </record>

        <!-- ── MANAGER ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
             Top-level role. Can do everything a Supervisor can, plus:
               - Full inventory management (create/edit products)
               - Validate worktags
               - Access all accounting and reporting features
               - Full timesheet administration

             Implies Supervisor so managers automatically get all
             supervisor and technician permissions.
        -->
        <record id="group_manager" model="res.groups">
            <field name="name">Manager</field>
            <field name="category_id" ref="module_category_techservices"/>
            <field name="implied_ids" eval="[
                (4, ref('techservices_groups.group_supervisor')),
                (4, ref('stock.group_stock_manager')),
                (4, ref('hr_timesheet.group_timesheet_manager')),
                (4, ref('account.group_account_manager')),
                (4, ref('base.group_system')),
            ]"/>
        </record>

    </data>
</odoo>

content.text:
Fixed. The root cause and the change made:

**Root cause:** `group_sale_salesman` ("Own Documents Only") carries a record rule — `sale.sale_order_personal_rule` — that limits `sale.order` reads to `user_id = current user OR user_id = False`. When the Project module loaded timesheets linked to sale order 57 (assigned to a different user), it was silently blocked by that rule.

**Fix:** Swapped `group_sale_salesman` → `group_sale_salesman_all_leads` ("All Documents") in the Supervisor's `implied_ids`. This group has the `sale.sale_order_see_all` rule (`domain = [(1,'=',1)]`) instead, giving the Supervisor unrestricted read access to all sale orders — which is appropriate since Supervisors manage the full pipeline.

2. Key Technical Concepts:
   - Odoo 18 custom module development (`techservices_groups`, `instrument_registry`)
   - `ir.model.access` — additive OR logic; cannot deny via new rules, must modify existing ones
   - `ir.rule` (record rules) — domain-based per-group restrictions on specific records
   - Odoo view inheritance via XPath with `position="attributes"` and `position="replace"`
   - XPath restrictions: `[@string]` and certain other attributes cannot be used as selectors
   - `groups="..."` attribute on view elements for server-side visibility control
   - `selection_add` with `ondelete` lambda for extending Selection fields
   - `_inherits` on `product.product` → `product.template` (custom template fields accessible directly on product.product)
   - Odoo `company_type` field: computed from `is_company`, inverse via `_write_company_type`
   - `sales_team.group_sale_salesman` ("Own Documents Only") vs `sales_team.group_sale_salesman_all_leads` ("All Documents") — the former carries a record rule blocking cross-user sale.order reads
   - Server-side action guards using `self.env.user.has_group()`
   - Docker-based Odoo: upgrade via `docker exec odoo18_dev odoo -u <module> --stop-after-init -d techservices`, restart with `docker compose restart odoo`

<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<odoo>
    <data noupdate="0">

        <!-- ── MODULE CATEGORY ──────────────────────────────────────────────
             Creates a "Technical Services" section in the user settings form.
             This groups our three roles together cleanly.
        -->
        <record id="module_category_techservices" model="ir.module.category">
            <field name="name">Technical Services</field>
            <field name="description">Roles for the Technical Services facility</field>
            <field name="sequence">20</field>
        </record>

        <!-- ── TECHNICIAN ───────────────────────────────────────────────────
             Base role. Can:
               - View and edit their assigned repair orders
               - View repair history for all instruments (read-only)
               - Add parts and timesheet lines to their repairs
               - Browse inventory catalog (read-only by default)
               - Log their own timesheets

             Implied groups give them the minimum Odoo access needed
             without exposing Sales or Accounting.
        -->
        <record id="group_technician" model="res.groups">
            <field name="name">Technician</field>
            <field name="category_id" ref="module_category_techservices"/>
            <field name="implied_ids" eval="[
                (4, ref('stock.group_stock_user')),
                (4, ref('hr_timesheet.group_hr_timesheet_user')),
            ]"/>
        </record>

        <!-- ── SUPERVISOR ───────────────────────────────────────────────────
             Mid-level role. Can do everything a Technician can, plus:
               - View and edit all repair orders
               - Create and manage sale orders
               - Create and manage worktags
               - View invoices

             Implies Technician so supervisors automatically get all
             technician permissions.

             NOTE: group_sale_salesman_all_leads ("User: All Documents") is used
             instead of group_sale_salesman ("User: Own Documents Only").
             The "Own Documents Only" group carries a record rule that restricts
             sale.order reads to orders where the user is the salesperson.
             This blocks the project/timesheet module from reading linked sale
             orders that belong to other users (e.g. orders created by an admin).
             "All Documents" lifts that restriction while keeping full sales access.
        -->
        <record id="group_supervisor" model="res.groups">
            <field name="name">Supervisor</field>
            <field name="category_id" ref="module_category_techservices"/>
            <field name="implied_ids" eval="[
                (4, ref('techservices_groups.group_technician')),
                (4, ref('sales_team.group_sale_salesman_all_leads')),
                (4, ref('hr_timesheet.group_hr_timesheet_approver')),
                (4, ref('account.group_account_invoice')),
            ]"/>
        </record>

        <!-- ── MANAGER ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
             Top-level role. Can do everything a Supervisor can, plus:
               - Full inventory management (create/edit products)
               - Validate worktags
               - Access all accounting and reporting features
               - Full timesheet administration

             Implies Supervisor so managers automatically get all
             supervisor and technician permissions.

        <!--
            INVOICE CONFIRM / POST BUTTON RESTRICTION
            ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

            Goal: Supervisors can create draft invoices but cannot post them.
            Only the Manager role should be able to move an invoice from
            Draft → Posted by clicking Confirm (customer invoices) or Post
            (journal entries).

            Both the "Confirm" and "Post" buttons call action_post() and share
            name="action_post", so a single XPath catches both.  We replace the
            existing groups="account.group_account_invoice" with
            groups="techservices_groups.group_manager", which is implied by
            the Manager role only.

            A matching server-side guard in models/account_move.py ensures the
            restriction also applies if action_post() is triggered outside the
            UI (e.g. RPC call or automated action).
        -->
        <record id="account_move_hide_post_supervisor" model="ir.ui.view">
            <field name="name">account.move.hide.post.supervisor.techservices</field>
            <field name="model">account.move</field>
            <field name="inherit_id" ref="account.view_move_form"/>
            <field name="arch" type="xml">
                <!-- Restrict both the "Confirm" (invoice) and "Post" (journal entry)
                     buttons to the Manager role.  Supervisors will see neither button
                     and therefore cannot transition an invoice out of Draft state. -->
                <xpath expr="//button[@name='action_post']" position="attributes">
                    <attribute name="groups">techservices_groups.group_manager</attribute>
                </xpath>
            </field>
        </record>
    </data>
</odoo>

import odoo
from odoo import api, models, fields
from odoo.http import request
from odoo.addons.mail.tools.discuss import Store


class IrHttp(models.AbstractModel):
    _inherit = 'ir.http'

    def session_info(self):
        """Override to add the current user data (partner or guest) if applicable."""
        result = super().session_info()
        store = Store()
        ResUsers = self.env["res.users"]

import odoo

from odoo.http import request
from odoo.addons.mail.tools.discuss import Store


class IrHttp(models.AbstractModel):

The asset is registered. Here's a summary of what was implemented:

**How it works:**

1. **`models/ir_http.py`** — Overrides `session_info()` to inject `techservices_messaging_disabled: True` into the page's session object for any user who is a Technician or Supervisor (but not Manager). This is computed once at login, server-side, so no async calls are needed in JavaScript.

2. **`static/src/hide_messaging_menu.js`** — Loads after `@mail/core/public_web/messaging_menu` (enforced by the import), checks `session.techservices_messaging_disabled`, and if true, removes the `"mail.messaging_menu"` entry from the systray registry. The NavBar reads this registry when rendering, so the chat/channel icon never appears.

**Result:**
- `meshead@chem.ubc.ca` (Supervisor) → messaging menu hidden
- `tech1, tech3` (Technicians) → messaging menu hidden  
- `seb@chem.ubc.ca` (Manager) → messaging menu visible as normal

The Discuss app itself was already restricted to `base.group_erp_manager`, so the full chat/channel app was already inaccessible — this change completes the picture by also removing the top-bar messaging panel.

No tests exist yet. Here's my recommendation:

---

## Testing approach for this module

Odoo's built-in test framework (`TransactionCase`) is the right tool — tests run in a transaction that's rolled back after each test, so they never touch live data. You'd create a `tests/` directory in `techservices_groups` with one file per workflow area.

### What to test

There are five distinct workflows worth covering:

**1. Access control — repair orders**
- Technician: can read repair orders, **cannot** create them → expect `AccessError`
- Supervisor: can create, read, write, delete repair orders
- Manager: same as Supervisor

**2. Access control — invoice posting**
- Supervisor: can create a draft invoice, **cannot** call `action_post()` → expect `UserError`
- Manager: can post invoices successfully

**3. Role inheritance**
- Supervisor automatically has Technician permissions (implied groups)
- Manager automatically has Supervisor + Technician permissions

**4. Product custom fields**
- Creating a product with `x_make`, `x_supplier_id`, `x_supplier_part_number` stores correctly
- The `x_supplier_id` domain correctly filters to `is_supplier=True` contacts only

**5. Supplier contact type**
- Creating a contact with `company_type='supplier'` sets `is_company=True` and `is_supplier=True`
- Changing away from `supplier` clears `is_supplier`
- The `ondelete` lambda fires correctly on group removal

### Structure

```
custom_modules/techservices_groups/
├── tests/
│   ├── __init__.py
│   ├── common.py          ← shared setUp: create 3 test users with the 3 roles
│   ├── test_repair_access.py
│   ├── test_invoice_access.py
│   ├── test_role_inheritance.py
│   ├── test_product_fields.py
│   └── test_supplier_contact.py
```

### How to run

```bash
docker exec odoo18_dev odoo \
  --test-enable \
  --test-tags techservices_groups \
  --stop-after-init \
  -d techservices
```

---

Would you like me to implement this? I can write all five test files now. The only decision is whether you want tests to run against the live `techservices` DB (using `SavepointCase` / `TransactionCase` which roll back automatically) or a fresh test DB — the live DB is fine for this since Odoo isolates every test in a savepoint.

content.text:
Good. Two things need to move: the **code** (the `odoo-dev` folder) and the **database** (the `techservices` Postgres volume). Here's the complete procedure:

---

## On your current machine

**Step 1 — Dump the database**
```bash
docker exec odoo18_db pg_dump -U odoo techservices > ~/Desktop/techservices.sql
```

**Step 2 — Copy everything to the new machine**

Copy two things:
- The entire `odoo-dev/` folder (contains `docker-compose.yml`, `custom_modules/`, `config/`)
- The dump file `techservices.sql`

Use AirDrop, an external drive, or `rsync` over SSH — whichever is fastest for you.

---

## On your new machine

**Step 3 — Install Docker Desktop**

Download from [docker.com](https://www.docker.com/products/docker-desktop/) and launch it.

**Step 4 — Start the containers (DB first, without Odoo)**

```bash
cd ~/Documents/Developer/odoo-dev   # wherever you put the folder
docker compose up -d db
```

Wait ~10 seconds for Postgres to initialize.

**Step 5 — Restore the database**

```bash
# Create the empty database
docker exec odoo18_db createdb -U odoo techservices

# Restore the dump
cat ~/Desktop/techservices.sql | docker exec -i odoo18_db psql -U odoo -d techservices
```

**Step 6 — Start Odoo**

```bash
docker compose up -d odoo
```

Open `http://localhost:8069` — it should come up with all your data and custom modules intact.

---

## Verify it's working

```bash
# Confirm the custom modules are loaded
docker exec odoo18_dev odoo --stop-after-init -d techservices 2>&1 | grep "techservices_groups\|instrument_registry"
```

If you see the modules listed without errors, you're good. The `config/odoo.conf` already points to the right addons path, so no config changes are needed.

Good picture. The repo already has git set up with 5 commits, and there's a batch of uncommitted work from our recent sessions. Here's the full plan:

---

## Step 1 — Create the GitHub repo

Go to [github.com/new](https://github.com/new) and create a new **private** repository. Name it something like `odoo-dev`. Do **not** initialize it with a README (the local repo already has one). Copy the repo URL (e.g. `https://github.com/sebastianmedrano/odoo-dev.git`).

---

## Step 2 — Commit all uncommitted work

Run these in the terminal from inside `odoo-dev/`:

```bash
cd ~/Documents/Developer/odoo-dev
```

```bash
git add \
  config/odoo.conf \
  custom_modules/techservices_groups/ \
  custom_modules/instrument_registry/models/service_instrument.py \
  custom_modules/instrument_registry/security/ir.model.access.csv \
  docs/
```

```bash
git commit -m "techservices_groups: add full role/access/UI/messaging restrictions and Department Unit field"
```

---

## Step 3 — Add the remote and push

Replace the URL with your actual repo URL:

```bash
git remote add origin https://github.com/sebastianmedrano/odoo-dev.git
git push -u origin main
```

It will ask for your GitHub username and password. For the password, use a **Personal Access Token** (not your GitHub account password) — you can generate one at GitHub → Settings → Developer settings → Personal access tokens → Tokens (classic) → Generate new token. Give it `repo` scope.

---

## One thing to be aware of

`config/odoo.conf` contains `db_password = odoo_dev_password`. Since this is a local dev password it's fine to commit, but if you ever move toward a staging or production environment, that file should be added to `.gitignore` and replaced with an example template. Let me know if you want me to set that up now.

message.content: What's the workflow for me to be able to work in different computers or even in my production server, and then commit in github and be able to extend my changes into all the versions in different systems. I'm a very new user of git

content.text:
Here's the mental model first, then the daily commands.

---

## The mental model

GitHub is the **single source of truth**. Every computer (your work Mac, home Mac, production server) is just a local copy. The flow is always:

```
GitHub  ←──push──  your computer
GitHub  ──pull──→  your computer
```

You never copy files between computers directly — GitHub is the middleman.

---

## Recommended branch structure for your situation

```
main   ← stable, production-ready code only
dev    ← where you develop and test (what you have now)
```

When something on `dev` is tested and ready, you merge it into `main` and deploy from `main` to the production server.

---

## Daily workflow on any computer

**Start of every work session — always pull first:**
```bash
git pull origin dev
```

**After making changes — save your work to GitHub:**
```bash
git add custom_modules/techservices_groups/   # stage what changed
git commit -m "brief description of what you did"
git push origin dev
```

**Switching to a different computer mid-work:**
Push on the first machine, then pull on the second. That's it.

---

## When something is ready for production

```bash
git checkout main
git merge dev
git push origin main
```

Then on the production server:
```bash
git pull origin main
docker exec odoo18_dev odoo -u techservices_groups --stop-after-init -d techservices
docker compose restart odoo
```

---

## The golden rule

**Always pull before you start working.** If you forget and make changes on two computers without syncing, git will warn you about conflicts — fixable, but annoying. Pulling first prevents it entirely.

message.content: As a separate challenge, I undestand the claude code has the major benefit of maintaining the memory of our work sessions. Can I close this terminal window and get back to you without you loosing contexts or needing to rebuild your memory?

content.text:
Yes — closing the terminal doesn't affect memory. Claude Code saves context in two places:

1. **Memory files** at `~/.claude/projects/.../memory/` — these persist across sessions and contain notes about your project, your preferences, and the decisions we've made together.

2. **Conversation history** — Claude Code stores recent session transcripts so I can pick up where we left off.

When you start a new session in the same project directory, I'll automatically reload that context. You may need to give me a brief "we were working on X" prompt to orient me if the last session was a while ago, but you won't need to re-explain the whole project from scratch.

What you **will** lose by closing the terminal is any running process (like a Docker container you started from that terminal), but the containers themselves keep running in the background regardless — that's what `restart: unless-stopped` in your `docker-compose.yml` does.

message.content: I'll be working on two computers and I want to be able to use this session's context, memory, etc. How can I do that?

content.text:
Claude Code's memory is stored locally on your machine at `~/.claude/`. It doesn't sync automatically between computers.

The simplest way to share it is to add that folder to your GitHub repo:

```bash
cp -r ~/.claude/projects/ ~/Documents/Developer/odoo-dev/.claude-memory/
```

Then commit and push it:

```bash
git add .claude-memory/
git commit -m "add claude memory for project context"
git push origin dev
```

On the second computer, after cloning/pulling:

```bash
cp -r ~/Documents/Developer/odoo-dev/.claude-memory/ ~/.claude/projects/
```

**However**, there's a simpler alternative that requires no setup: just start a new session on the second computer in the same project directory. I'll have the memory files if you copy them over, but even without them I can quickly rebuild context by reading the codebase — the code itself tells most of the story. A single sentence like "we were adding reporting features to the techservices_groups module" is usually enough to orient me.

Which approach works better for you depends on how frequently you switch machines. If it's daily, syncing the memory folder is worth it. If it's occasional, a brief prompt is faster.

message.content: can you give me a bit more of contexts about what these commands do?

content.text:
Sure. Let me break down each command:

---

**`cp -r ~/.claude/projects/ ~/Documents/Developer/odoo-dev/.claude-memory/`**

- `cp` = copy
- `-r` = recursively (copy folders and everything inside them)
- `~/.claude/projects/` = where Claude Code stores its memory files on your Mac (notes about your project, preferences, decisions we've made)
- `~/Documents/Developer/odoo-dev/.claude-memory/` = a new folder inside your project directory where you're putting a copy of those memory files, so they travel with the repo

---

**`git add .claude-memory/`**

Tells git "I want to track this new folder." Git doesn't automatically track new files — you have to explicitly add them.

---

**`git commit -m "add claude memory for project context"`**

Saves a snapshot of the current state of those files into git history, with a descriptive message explaining what the snapshot contains.

---

**`git push origin dev`**

Uploads that snapshot to GitHub (`origin` = your GitHub repo, `dev` = the branch name).

---

**On the second computer:**

**`cp -r ~/Documents/Developer/odoo-dev/.claude-memory/ ~/.claude/projects/`**

The reverse — copies the memory files from the repo into the location where Claude Code expects to find them on that machine.

---

The net result: your Claude memory files live inside your git repo, so they stay in sync across machines the same way your code does — pull to get the latest, push to share updates.
